stemBlocks.value: Using a ruler, a pencil and a pair of compasses, construct the trapezium ABCD with AB = 8 cm, ∠BAD = 60°, AD = 6 cm, ∠ABC = 90° and AB parallel to CD. Credit is given for clearly drawn construction lines.
Think first: Build the two given angles on the fixed side AB first; the parallel condition then decides where C must sit.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p158-q14 from workbook page 158.

solutionSteps.instruction: Construct a 60° angle at A and mark D on its arm with AD = 6 cm.

contentBlocks.value: Standard 60° arc construction, then compasses set to 6 cm from A

solutionSteps.instruction: Construct a perpendicular to AB at B, on the same side as D.

contentBlocks.value: Equal arcs each side of B, then equal larger arcs crossing above B

solutionSteps.instruction: Construct the line through D parallel to AB.

contentBlocks.value: Copy the 60° angle at D on the other side of AD, or mark the equal perpendicular distance above AB
Result: line through D parallel to AB

solutionSteps.instruction: Mark C where that parallel meets the perpendicular from B, then join DC and BC.

contentBlocks.value: Check by measurement: DC ≈ 5 cm and BC ≈ 5.2 cm

strategyBlocks.value: Draw AB = 8 cm, construct 60° at A and mark AD = 6 cm, construct the perpendicular at B, then draw the line through D parallel to AB and let it cut that perpendicular at C.

finalAnswerBlocks.value: A correctly drawn trapezium ABCD with AB = 8 cm, AD = 6 cm, ∠BAD = 60°, ∠ABC = 90° and DC parallel to AB. Accuracy checks: DC ≈ 5 cm and BC ≈ 5.2 cm (= 6 sin 60°).

whyThisWorks.value: The two given angles at the ends of AB fix the directions of AD and BC, and the given length AD fixes D. Requiring DC parallel to AB forces D and C to lie the same perpendicular distance above AB, so C is the single point where that line crosses the perpendicular from B. The height 6 sin 60° ≈ 5.20 cm and the horizontal shift 6 cos 60° = 3 cm are what make DC = 8 − 3 = 5 cm.

commonErrors.misconception: Making CD parallel to AD instead of to AB.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Making CD parallel to AD instead of to AB.

examTip.value: Label vertices strictly in the order given (A, B, C, D around the shape) before you draw — most lost marks in construction come from a correctly built figure with the wrong letters on it.
